title: Model Hangar
intro: Open models you can run yourself. Clearing the Six Gates earns launch clearance, but the gates still apply to every real deployment: walk them again for each use case.
caveat: Compiled from the publishers' public model cards when this catalog was written. Newer versions may exist and licences can change: read the model card before you download or deploy. "Open weights" means the trained model is downloadable; "fully open" also publishes the training data and code. Custom licences are not OSI-approved open-source licences.

runtime.name: Ollama
steps: Install Ollama from ollama.com and start it (it listens on http://localhost:11434).
Pull a model from the hangar, e.g. `ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b`.
Start the HumanSI server with `HUMANSI_OLLAMA_URL=http://localhost:11434 go run ./cmd/humansi`.
Fly the Six Gates, earn clearance, and open the console.

models.name: OLMo 2
models.note: Weights, training data and training code are all published: the most inspectable family in the hangar.

models.name: Mistral 7B
models.note: A compact general model. Mistral publishes other models under different licences, so check each card.

models.name: Qwen2.5
models.licence: Apache 2.0 for most sizes (some sizes use the Qwen licence)
models.note: Ships in many sizes; the 0.5B variant runs on modest laptops and is the quickest way to test the console.

models.name: Phi-4
models.note: A small model focused on reasoning.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.licence: MIT (the smaller distilled variants inherit their Qwen or Llama base licence)
models.note: A reasoning model. The full model is very large; the distilled sizes are what most laptops can run.

models.name: Gemma 3
models.licence: Gemma Terms of Use (custom, with a prohibited-use policy)
models.note: Open weights under Google's own terms rather than an OSI licence.

models.name: Llama 3.2
models.licence: Llama 3.2 Community License (custom, with an acceptable-use policy)
models.note: Widely supported; the licence adds conditions that OSI licences do not.
